questions.q: How does the summary define resilience?
a: The ability to bounce back from adversity
The habit of avoiding situations that cause pain
A talent that only a few people are born with
The confidence that nothing bad will ever happen
questions.why: The overview calls resilience the ability to bounce back from adversity and stresses that it can be learned.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest you should treat hardship?
a: As a natural part of life that can be faced with bravery
As a sign that you have chosen the wrong path
As something to hide from friends and family
As a problem that only willpower can erase
questions.why: Lesson 1 says accepting hardship as a normal part of life is an essential truth that makes things easier to handle.

questions.q: What does the author say you should do when you miss your plans or targets?
a: Take responsibility for the failure
Lower the target immediately
Wait for motivation to return
Blame circumstances outside your control
questions.why: Lesson 2 says that when you fall short you should own the failure, because building your life is up to you.

questions.q: According to the summary, what helps resilience grow over time?
a: Reflecting on mistakes and setting meaningful goals
Avoiding all risk until you feel completely ready
Comparing your progress with other people
Keeping your goals private and vague
questions.why: Lesson 3 pairs honest reflection on failure with goals that give your life purpose and drive.

questions.q: Why does the summary recommend goals that genuinely inspire you?
a: They make hardship easier to face and give life purpose
They guarantee that you will never fail again
They remove the need for daily habits
They impress other people more than small goals do
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues you are more likely to endure hardship when you are working toward something that matters to you.
